proposal.name: Verify ordinary code one component at a time

issue_plan.name: Verify ordinary code one component at a time
issue_plan.summary: These first ten issues let developers check unchanged Go and Python against a model, then prove selected functions in their own packages while ordinary surrounding code keeps its style. They add tested contracts for dependencies the provers cannot handle, runtime checks of callers during tests, and receipts that distinguish each component's proof, assumptions, model tests, and unchecked behavior. A comparison against base-branch evidence prevents CI from silently accepting weaker guarantees. Factory drafting, synthesis, and scope support for this adoption path, wiring this repository's protected workflow, and a real-codebase pilot such as ask3d remain after these ten issues.

issues.title: Record verification evidence for each component
issues.body:
Issue #210 requires incremental verification inside ordinary Go and Python: selecting one function for proof must not label its surrounding application proved. Today internal/project/project.go describes one code directory and internal/verify/verify.go sets project assurance to proved whenever a Code result exists, even when it lists unverified functions. Establish the component configuration and evidence representation on which later language support can build.

Give components stable, qualified identities tied to their real package, symbol, and source. Validate explicit proof selections and associations with contracts, tests, and conformance drivers; duplicate or unresolved selections must not silently disappear. Account for unselected code in the declared source scope as unchecked unless evidence actually covers it, and make the scope itself visible. Preserve existing manifests and their checks through an explicit compatibility path. Configuration declares intended checks; only successful tool results establish assurance.

Extend JSON reports, fingerprints, Markdown receipts, and existing summary consumers, including the dashboard, to show proved, trusted and tested, tested against the model, and unchecked components. Keep proof, bounded or sampled conformance, runtime checks, and trusted assumptions as separate evidence so later issues can populate them without collapsing them into one score. A proof of one component must not promote neighboring functions, and at-every-size wording must apply only where its existing evidence requirements hold. Include source and contract identities in evidence fingerprints.

Acceptance should cover a mixed package, same-named methods on different receivers or classes, unchecked neighbors, failed or missing proof output, deterministic fingerprints, and legacy Go, Python, and TypeScript receipts. Update SPEC.md and README descriptions affected by this change under D-0122; the merger records the decision supporting the new component claims because plumbing builds cannot write decisions/. Keep ratified model statements unchanged.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Build Python test images from the application's requirements
issues.body:
Issue #210 requires checking existing Python applications with third-party dependencies. internal/toolchain/deps.go currently builds only npm dependency images, while Python tests and conformance run in a standard-library-only image. Add the Python dependency image path that subsequent existing-code and contract-test support will use.

Build from the application's own requirements and a pinned Python base, and identify the effective dependency environment in the receipt. Cache reuse must depend on the recipe and every effective dependency input, including referenced requirement and constraint files. Record the resolved dependency artifacts sufficiently to distinguish environments when requirements are not fully pinned; document supported requirement forms and reproducibility handling in this issue's implementation plan. Do not silently fall back to a standard-library-only environment when installation fails. Installation may use network during image construction, as the TypeScript path does; tests and conformance execute offline with no host environment or credentials.

Integrate the image selection and evidence with Python execution and the component receipt foundation. Keep the application dependency environment distinct from the pinned Nagini verifier environment: an application package must not replace the prover's own dependencies. Projects without requirements retain their supported standard-library path. Application dependency files are inputs, not files the gate rewrites.

Acceptance should build and reuse an image for a small real third-party dependency, invalidate it when an effective requirements input changes, report installation failures, and demonstrate offline execution using the installed package. Add an integration fixture for a referenced requirements or constraints file and verify recipe provenance in the receipt. Update SPEC.md and README under D-0122, with the dependency-policy decision recorded by the merger.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Check unchanged Go packages against a model
issues.body:
Provide the first adoption step from issue #210 for Go: a developer adds a ratified TLA+ model and a conformance adapter for an existing application, then checks the real application without changing its source or proving any function. Build on the component evidence representation. Existing-code validation in internal/project/project.go currently accepts only TypeScript, and the Go path in internal/verify/language.go always calls Gobra and expects a standalone project module with an explorer.

Add an explicit Go conformance-only path using the application's actual module and package context. Stage a throwaway copy with the local imports, resources, and existing go.mod/go.sum dependencies needed to run the checked code. Resolve dependencies before offline execution and identify those inputs in the receipt. Allow the verification project to sit inside an existing module; do not require production code to export Init, Try, Abstract, or a comparable State type. The separate adapter may provide the model-facing interface. Avoid Gobra's current fallback that proves every Go file when no file marker exists.

Drive the surrounding application operations, read state back from the real implementation, and pass their traces to the existing conformance checks. Establish that the adapter executes the named application code rather than a duplicate implementation, and hash that code. Retain bounded/sample claims and the existing stronger requirements for an exhaustive driver and attempted-step coverage. Only components covered by this evidence become tested against the model. Existing proved standalone projects keep their proof and agreement paths.

Acceptance should start with an unchanged idiomatic Go package containing sibling imports and an existing module dependency, pass a valid lifecycle, reject a forbidden transition, and reject an adapter that ignores the named implementation. Confirm original application bytes are unchanged and unsupported prover syntax in ordinary code causes no style rejection. Update SPEC.md and README to document this manual CLI adoption path and its evidence limits; the merger records the change to the standalone-module and proof-first policies. Factory issue routing and synthesis are deferred beyond this ten-issue tranche.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Check unchanged Python applications against a model
issues.body:
Provide issue #210's initial adoption path for Python using the component evidence and Python dependency images introduced earlier. A developer adds a ratified model and conformance driver alongside an existing application, while the application remains unchanged and no function needs Nagini annotations. Today existing-code projects are TypeScript-only, package discovery looks for package-lock.json, and Python execution copies only the verification project.

Extend project validation, package discovery, staging, and language routing to execute named Python application code in its own package context. Preserve local imports and required resources, use the application's requirements image, and run its configured tests and driver offline in the throwaway workspace. Bind and hash the actual source exercised by the driver; a driver that substitutes its own state machine must not establish evidence for the application. The gate must neither require # +nagini markers nor send ordinary modules to Nagini in this mode.

The driver must exercise surrounding application behavior, including its calls into the modeled component, and read observations from that implementation. Reuse TLC trace checking, deterministic runs, and the existing exhaustive and attempted-step checks where the driver claims those properties. Report only tested-against-the-model evidence at this stage, with the actual bounds and sampling scope, and leave uncovered components unchecked.

Acceptance should use an unchanged ordinary Python package with a sibling import and a real installed third-party dependency. A valid task lifecycle passes, an invalid transition fails conformance, a driver that never uses the selected code fails, and runtime/import errors cannot yield successful evidence. Verify unchanged source bytes and preserve existing Python and TypeScript behavior. Update SPEC.md and README under D-0122 and have the merger record the existing-code policy extension. Factory drafting and synthesis support remain for a later tranche.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Give trusted dependency contracts executed test evidence
issues.body:
Issue #210 allows a proved component to call behavior Gobra or Nagini cannot verify, including standard-library operations, maps, I/O, and third-party packages, only through explicit trusted contracts backed by tests. Add the shared contract inventory and test-evidence path before wiring either prover to it. Build on component identities and the Go/Python application sandboxes from the earlier issues.

Bind each trusted contract to the real operation or dependency it describes, the exact contract content, source or dependency version, and the tests intended to support it. Tests must exercise the real implementation of that boundary and check its specified outcomes; testing only a substitute stub does not support a contract about the real dependency. Run the selected tests in the application's environment, record which actually ran and passed, and fail required evidence when tests are missing, skipped, or fail. Report these boundaries as trusted and tested, never proved.

Extend receipts and fingerprints with contract content identities, backing test identities and outcomes, and links from relying components when a prover supplies those links. Keep declarations distinct from proof assumptions actually used: the later Gobra and Nagini issues will collect those dependencies from their verification inputs. This issue must not fabricate proof results or certify an unused declaration as a checked call boundary. Provide a common way for those adapters to report missing or unaccounted-for assumptions.

Acceptance should cover a passing and failing real dependency contract in both languages, a missing or skipped backing test, changed contract and dependency inputs, and a declared contract that no proof has used. Tests should check observable preconditions, results, mutations, and error outcomes relevant to their contract. Update SPEC.md and README to explain that dependency contracts remain assumptions supported by tests, with the supporting decision recorded by the merger under D-0122.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Prove selected Go functions in their existing package
issues.body:
Implement issue #210's Go proof step on top of existing-code conformance, component receipts, and tested trusted contracts. A developer must be able to annotate and select a critical function where it already lives, with Gobra proving that implementation against its contract. internal/gobra/gobra.go currently selects entire files and mounts only the code directory; this must no longer force the selected function into a separate core or require its ordinary neighbors to adopt Gobra's style.

Verify selected functions and required verified helpers with the real package's declarations, types, and import context. Preserve the connection between the proof input and the actual selected source: any generated verifier input must faithfully represent that implementation, not a separately maintained copy. A same-file ordinary function using unsupported constructs must remain outside the proof boundary. Calls the prover cannot handle cross an explicit trusted-contract boundary, using the shared test evidence. Include representative standard-library, map, I/O, and third-party boundaries in the supported path rather than requiring a whole application rewrite.

Report exactly which symbols were proved, the contracts they satisfy, overflow checking, and every trusted assumption the proofs use. Missing or undeclared assumptions and failed selected proofs fail the gate; unrelated unselected code does not fail merely for its style. Continue running conformance on the real surrounding application. Attribute proof only to selected verified components and keep their conditional assumptions and tested interactions visible.

Acceptance must run the pinned Gobra image on an existing package containing a selected function and an unsupported ordinary neighbor in the same file, with an actual call through a tested trusted contract. Mutating the function to violate its contract, removing a necessary trusted contract, or breaking its backing test must fail. Confirm the proof concerns the source that tests and conformance execute, preserves ordinary neighbors, and does not weaken existing Gobra projects. Update SPEC.md and README and record the revised proof-boundary decision through the merger.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Prove selected Python functions in their existing package
issues.body:
Implement issue #210's Python proof step using the existing-application path and tested trusted-contract inventory. A developer selects and annotates a critical Python function in its actual module; Nagini proves that function without requiring a separate core.py or annotations on ordinary surrounding code. internal/verify/nagini.go currently selects whole # +nagini files and stages only the code directory.

Add selection and verifier input construction that preserves the selected function's implementation, types, and package context while excluding unrelated ordinary function bodies, including neighbors in the same file that Nagini cannot handle. Do not claim a proof of a detached reimplementation as a proof of application code. Resolve calls beyond the proof boundary through explicit trusted contracts for the relevant standard-library, map, I/O, and third-party behavior. Keep the pinned Nagini environment separate from the application's dependency image used for tests and conformance.

Collect exact proved symbols and every assumed contract actually used, connect them to executed backing tests, and include them in component receipts and fingerprints. An unresolved dependency boundary, failed selected proof, or failed required contract test must fail. Ordinary unselected modules retain their natural syntax. Run conformance against the real application with its installed dependencies and keep tested surrounding behavior separate from proof evidence. Preserve the supported legacy marked-file projects.

Acceptance must run the pinned Nagini verifier on an existing application with a selected function and an unsupported ordinary neighbor in the same module, including a real tested dependency boundary. A function-body contract violation, an omitted trusted contract, and a failing backing test must each be rejected. Confirm the selected source is the implementation executed in the application environment and that no unrelated application function changes. Update SPEC.md and README to explain in-place Python proof and its trust boundary, with the policy decision recorded by the merger.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Check Go callers against proved component contracts during tests
issues.body:
Issue #210 requires checking how ordinary Go code uses a proved component. Build on in-place Go proofs and existing-code conformance by enforcing the selected component's boundary contract on every invocation executed during the configured application tests and conformance runs. Ordinary callers must need neither annotations nor manual calls to a shadow model or wrapper.

Place test-time checks at the actual component boundary so calls through surrounding code, method values, and function values cannot bypass them simply by avoiding the conformance driver's call site. Check entry obligations before the operation and executable result, mutation, and error obligations at the correct exit, preserving arguments, return values, side effects, and panic behavior. Any instrumentation belongs in the throwaway test workspace and must retain the identity of the source proved by Gobra.

This issue's ratified implementation plan must define the executable interpretation of supported boundary contracts, including entry snapshots, and the treatment of proof-only constructs such as permissions and quantifiers. A clause that cannot be faithfully checked must be explicit unresolved or trusted evidence; it cannot be silently dropped while the receipt claims the full contract was checked. Complete runtime checking requires every required executable boundary obligation to be evaluated on each exercised invocation. An unresolved required check fails this gate stage; proof-only assumptions remain separately visible. The evidence applies to calls exercised in tests, not all possible executions.

Acceptance should include an unannotated application caller violating a precondition, a result or state violation, and calls through a method or function value. Valid execution retains its behavior, violations fail the gate with component and contract diagnostics, and an unexercised component gains no runtime-call evidence. Demonstrate conformance through the surrounding orchestration as well: a caller can satisfy a function contract yet take a model-forbidden sequence, which must still fail conformance. Update receipts, SPEC.md, and README with these separate evidence limits and have the merger record the runtime-contract decision.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Check Python callers against proved component contracts during tests
issues.body:
Issue #210 requires runtime checking of ordinary Python callers of proved functions. Build on in-place Nagini proof and existing-application conformance. The current internal/verify/naginiruntime/nagini_contracts/contracts.py makes Requires and Ensures no-ops and does not implement entry snapshots or result semantics, so importing that stand-in does not establish caller correctness.

Enforce selected boundary contracts on every invocation exercised by the configured application tests and conformance runs without editing or annotating ordinary callers. Instrument the actual function or method boundary in the throwaway runtime workspace so existing imports, aliases, and bound methods receive the checks. Preserve application behavior, dependency imports, returned values, mutations, and exceptions. Evaluate entry obligations before the body and result, state, and declared exception obligations at the correct exit, with faithful Old and Result semantics where supported.

The ratified implementation plan for this issue must define executable contract semantics and account explicitly for permission predicates, quantifiers, and other proof-only clauses. Unsupported obligations must not disappear behind a no-op while a receipt claims full runtime enforcement; report unresolved or tested trusted obligations distinctly, and claim complete boundary checking only when every required executable obligation is evaluated on each exercised invocation. An unresolved required check fails this gate stage; proof-only assumptions remain separately visible. Bind runtime evidence to the same component source and contracts Nagini proved. Record exercised calls and failures, and make clear that tests establish nothing about unexecuted calls.

Acceptance should exercise an ordinary imported caller, an alias or bound method, a bad precondition, post-state or return failure, and the supported exception path. A passing application retains its behavior, each violation fails with a useful diagnostic, and zero exercised calls cannot yield runtime-check evidence. Include a surrounding orchestration trace that violates the model despite locally valid calls and ensure conformance catches it. Update component receipts, SPEC.md, and README and have the merger record the new runtime-contract semantics.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Fail CI when component evidence loses an established guarantee
issues.body:
Issue #210 requires incremental adoption without silently moving backwards. Build a base-aware evidence comparison for the component reports, trusted contracts, runtime checks, and conformance introduced by the preceding issues, expose it through the CLI, and wire it into the gate workflow emitted by internal/setup/gate.yml. Today CI discovers manifests only at HEAD and verifies them independently, so deleting a project or proof selection can make its earlier guarantee disappear.

Compare candidate evidence with independently obtained evidence for an explicit base revision, using the union of projects and component identities on both sides. The candidate must not choose a weaker baseline or omit a previously checked component to escape comparison. Compare evidence dimensions and their scope rather than ranking the four display labels: proof cannot be replaced by trusted tests, added proof does not excuse losing model conformance, and required contract tests or runtime boundary checks cannot disappear. Changes in contract meaning or trusted assumptions must be surfaced and must not pass merely because a label still says proved. Define deliberate contract revisions, component renames/removals, and first-adoption baseline handling in this issue's ratified plan, preserving the rule that lost guarantees fail CI.

Publish the affected component, previous evidence, candidate evidence, and reason for each regression. Tests must cover removal of a proof selector, a backing contract test, runtime checking, a conformance binding, and an entire manifest, plus adding proof to an existing model-tested component without losing other evidence. Use end-to-end fixtures for both Go and Python that start with unchanged-code conformance and advance to an in-place proof with a tested assumption and checked callers. Preserve TypeScript's conformance-only status and existing ratification and model-pin checks.

Update CLI documentation, SPEC.md, README, and the generated workflow template, with decisions recorded by the merger under D-0122. Plumbing plans cannot write .github/: document the exact invocation and baseline/artifact requirements for the subsequent maintainer issue that wires this repository's protected workflow. That repository workflow change, factory authoring and scope support, and a live application pilot remain outside these first ten issues; the generated workflow must enforce the comparison when installed.
